title: Flat localized presentation kernel intersection
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $S$ an $R$-algebra, $q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$, $n\in\mathbb N$, and $\varphi:P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow S$ a surjective $R$-algebra map [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Write $p=q\cap R$, $Q=\varphi^{-1}(q)$, $I=\ker\varphi$, and $A=P_Q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If the induced local ring homomorphism $R_p\to S_q$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then $IA\cap pA=(pA)(IA)$ as ideals of $A$. No finite-generation or complete-intersection hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 00SY, proof of (3) implies (2), equations and flatness paragraphs; Tag 00SC. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00SY and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00SC.

proof.text: Construct Rp=R_p, A=P_Q, B=S_q and their local ring maps a:Rp→A, b:Rp→B, l:A→B. The algebra-map compatibility φ∘(R→P)=R→S proves p=Q∩R and l∘a=b. Localization uniqueness (IsLocalization.ringHom_ext) proves the latter on fractions. Give A,B their a,b algebra structures; hflat is then exactly Module.Flat Rp B. Package l as an Rp-algebra map g. RingHom.surjectiveOnStalks_of_surjective and its localRingHom_surjective theorem give surjectivity. IsLocalization.ker_map with Ideal.map_primeCompl_comap_of_surjective gives ker l=IA. These are direct applications of the named Mathlib declarations, fully implemented in Lean.

Apply Mathlib LinearMap.ker_inf_smul_top_eq_smul_of_flat to g.toLinearMap and m=maximalIdeal Rp. Rewrite its kernel as (IA).restrictScalars Rp. Ideal.smul_top_eq_map and Ideal.smul_restrictScalars rewrite both products; IsLocalization.AtPrime.map_eq_maximalIdeal and Ideal.map_map identify mA with pA. Finally Submodule.restrictScalars_injective transports the underlying Rp-submodule equality back to the A-ideal equality IA∩pA=(pA)(IA). This is proved in Lean, using no project theorem.
